answer.note:
The four ref files are identical generic text, so I chose from the code. Suggested split of the 60 minutes: D 35, C 15, A 5, B 5.

D (dogwhistle/honest.py) is the match. `_verify_history` at honest.py:175-184 raises "ledger seal must be a separate commit" when `prereg_commit == ledger_commit`. It also requires `git diff --name-only` between the two commits to equal exactly `[public seal path]`, so the ledger-seal commit may change only the public digest file. I did not check the "two-arm" wording or run the tests. Spend the time on the rest of `_verify_history`, edge cases such as renames, and tests/test_honest.py.

C (dogwhistle/visibility.py) is the closest sibling. Its `_verify_history` at visibility.py:191-199 has the same structure but only checks ancestry, source files and the digest. It has no equal-commit rejection and no check on which files changed. Use it as the contrast case to confirm it is not the target.

A (study.py) and B (heldout.py) have a three-commit `verify_history` (prereg, seal, ledger). It checks ancestry, source files and digests only, with no equal-commit or changed-files check. A quick skim is enough.

The four ref files are identical generic text, so I chose from the code. Suggested split of the 60 minutes: D 35, C 15, A 5, B 5.

D (dogwhistle/honest.py) is the match. `_verify_history` at honest.py:175-184 raises "ledger seal must be a separate commit" when `prereg_commit == ledger_commit`. It also requires `git diff --name-only` between the two commits to equal exactly `[public seal path]`, so the ledger-seal commit may change only the public digest file. I did not check the "two-arm" wording or run the tests. Spend the time on the rest of `_verify_history`, edge cases such as renames, and tests/test_honest.py.

C (dogwhistle/visibility.py) is the closest sibling. Its `_verify_history` at visibility.py:191-199 has the same structure but only checks ancestry, source files and the digest. It has no equal-commit rejection and no check on which files changed. Use it as the contrast case to confirm it is not the target.

A (study.py) and B (heldout.py) have a three-commit `verify_history` (prereg, seal, ledger). It checks ancestry, source files and digests only, with no equal-commit or changed-files check. A quick skim is enough.
